top_story: As the Iran war tightened around the Strait of Hormuz, aid groups warned on 29 April that the blockade was choking deliveries of food, fuel, and medicine to millions, turning a military confrontation into a broad civilian emergency. This external escalation coincides with acute internal repression, with Narges Mohammadi’s continued imprisonment despite severe health decline underscoring a state prepared to absorb humanitarian and political costs at home as pressure mounts abroad. The immediate regional picture is one of shrinking space for de-escalation, where coercive posturing is amplifying both market shock and civilian suffering.
